Hyundai Reveals All 2027 Model Year Changes to American Lineup, Confirms All-New Tucson ICE & HEV
6 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The South Korean automaker has made it easier for all of us to track the modifications to the 2027MY lineup by compiling a list of changes for them – and we have two major confirmations along with a specialty model.
First, Hyundai has reconfirmed that the all-new NX5 fifth-generation Tucson is coming to America for the 2027 model year, packing the fresh “Art of Steel” design, more passenger and cargo space, both ICE and hybrid powertrains, and the next-generation Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Mechanically, the 2027 Tucson will use Hyundai’s 1.6-liter turbocharged GDI four-cylinder, producing 184 hp and 195 lb.-ft. of torque paired to an eight-speed automatic transmission. The 1.6L turbo hybrid system has a combined output of 233 hp and 280 lb-ft of torque, paired with a six-speed auto. Both are available with FWD or HTRAC all-wheel drive, and towing capacity is up to 2,500 lbs. on ICE models and 3,000 lbs. on the HEV.
The company, most importantly, said that the XRT PRO model is a hybrid-only, adventure-focused version with HTRAC AWD, a suspension lift, 8.3 inches of ground clearance, and 18-inch wheels plus all-terrain tires. It will include the X-Trek+ off-road technology “with real-time terrain assessment and Target Speed Control.”
The specialty novelty is the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 6 N, which is arriving during the spring season of 2027 with 601-hp dual-motor AWD, and up to 641 hp and 568 lb.-ft. of torque using N Grin Boost. The EV will sprint to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds with N Launch Control and has a 159-mph top speed. The 84.0-kWh battery is good for up to 245 miles of all-electric range, and thanks to the 800V platform, it can recharge 10–80% in approximately 18 minutes with a compatible 350-kW DC fast charger.
It also gets a standard NACS charging port and a CCS adapter, along with N Performance technology: the N e-Shift with simulated performance gear changes, N Active Sound+ with selectable performance sound profiles, N Launch Control, N Pedal, N Drift Optimizer, and more. The third major novelty for 2027 is the 2027 Hyundai Elantra – the eighth generation of the compact car series was launched in June 2026 as the Avante at the Busan International Mobility Show in Busan, South Korea, but the company is still keeping the Elantra details under wraps – most likely for a surprise premiere at the upcoming LA Auto Show (November 20-29).
The rest of the lineup is comprised of the 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 and 5 N (EV), Hyundai IONIQ 9 (EV), Hyundai Palisade (ICE, HEV), Hyundai Santa Fe (ICE, HEV), Hyundai Santa Cruz (ICE), Hyundai Kona (ICE), Hyundai Venue (ICE), which are carryover models with minor changes, and the Hyundai Sonata (ICE, HEV, N Line), which features no changes at all.

Networking
Meta OCP Summit-MetaRoCE 4
At OCP Summit 2026, we saw Meta’s new MetaRoCE network adapter. This is Meta’s answer to providing an open RDMA transport layer that has features like packet spraying, congestion control, and more. This was a presentation we saw at OCP Summit, but Meta had a NIC on display.
Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter at OCP 2026
Here is the display from the Meta booth at OCP Summit 2026, where you can see an OCP NIC 3.0 card.
Meta OCP Summit-MetaRoCE 1
During its OCP 2026 presentation, Meta shared some of the big features of MetaRoCE:
Per-path reliability and congestion control
Receiver rate hints (RCN) for fast incast convergence
Tolerates packet loss and reordering
Single QP carries multiple streams over multiple network paths
Runs on commodity Ethernet: ECN + ECMP, no switch (Source : Meta)
Meta OCP Summit-MetaRoCE 2
Before OCP Summit, Meta demonstrated this with the AMD Pensando NIC series. The programmability allowed it to implement the protocol without having dedicated hardware. That allows Meta to potentially source from multiple vendors.
Meta OCP Summit-MetaRoCE 3
Meta is trying to build a network protocol that can scale to million-GPU training, but also that can run on different network topologies and hardware.
Meta OCP Summit-MetaRoCE 5
As a quick aside, the NIC shown was an OCP NIC 3.0 with SFF pull tab design, which is our favorite form factor that we wish all server vendors used.
Final Words
Given Meta’s heritage of starting OCP Summit, they usually have super-cool hardware in the booth. Last year, we got the AMD Helios MI450 Rack at OCP Summit with a Different Version from Meta as an example. This year, the company brought some larger nodes, but also small items like this adapter. It is always neat to see what Meta is working on.
If you want to see what AWS is doing, for example, you can check out our Inside the Secretive AWS Networking Lab .

2027 Ford Racing Mustang For the NASCAR Cup Series Was Revealed Ahead of Feisty Veterans Day Race
12 photos
Photo: Ford
As part of the festivities centered around the Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic event, Ford showed us the new Ford Racing Mustang for the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series – and this time around it’s way more akin to a road car because it’s based on an actual customer vehicle, the 795-horsepower Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC .
The Blue Oval company had an incredibly eventful day on November 11 – during Veterans Day . The Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic was a huge event, taking place live at Daytona International Speedway, with Grammy-winning superstar Nelly in the musical lineup, Bobby Bones as the host, and a trio of NASCAR favorites from the USA Network on the call.
The Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic, of course, was tasked with creating a “real impact for military and veteran families,” so people could donate to the Proud to Honor Fund, supported by GlobalGiving and Ford Philanthropy. Naturally, the entertainment was at the highest levels possible, as the Most Patriotic Race at Daytona Has a Score to Settle was also part of the inaugural lineup.
For this race, no less than twelve Ford Racing drivers competed in six teams, each racing a Ford Mustang Dark Horse R with a custom livery inspired by a military branch's iconic vehicle, vessel, or aircraft. Inspired by the classic Army-Navy Game, the track race offered representation to all six branches of the US Armed Forces, with every Dark Horse R featuring a custom Ford Racing livery dedicated to their respective branch.
So, the Army had a Ford inspired by the Abrams tank, the Marine Corps by their Assault Amphibious Vehicle, the Navy by the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer, the Air Force by the F-22 Raptor, the Space Force by the X-37B Orbital Test Vehicle, and the Coast Guard by the Sentinel-class Fast Response Cutter.
In the end, Austin Cindric was the winner in the Air Force Team’s Ford Mustang Dark Horse R, followed by Robert Noaker from Team Marines and Ryan Preece from Team Navy. As for the Blue Oval, the Ford Motor Company took the opportunity to present to the Daytona audience the Mustang Dark Horse SC-based new Ford Racing Mustang that will compete in the NASCAR Cup Series starting with the upcoming 2027 season.
The S650 is easily recognizable now, bringing back the times when NASCAR was taking cars directly from the showroom onto oval racing tracks, and the Ford Racing Mustang has a new, “aggressive-looking nose that has been designed to optimize aerodynamics” instead of cooling like on the road car. It comes with additional downforce, and one can also notice quite easily the carbon fiber side sills with integrated exhaust when looking at the car from the profile.
The new Mustang will make its debut during Daytona Speedweeks, which culminates with the 69th annual edition of the Daytona 500 on February 21, 2027, and it’s only normal that the unveiling of the new Cup car was part of the events of the inaugural Ford Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic at Daytona International Speedway.
“When we introduced the Mustang Dark Horse SC in January and announced it was coming to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, we had no time to waste,” said Mark Rushbrook, global director, Ford Racing. “Racing makes our road cars better, and our road cars make our race cars better. We put that philosophy to work here, incorporating key elements from the Dark Horse SC into the new Mustang race car to help make it even more competitive every week.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ford Racing (@fordracing)

Nuclear-Powered NASA Moon Rover Is Made of Curiosity and Perseverance Parts, Launches in 2028
11 photos
Photo: NASA
Over the past weekend, American space agency NASA laid out new plans for the conquest and colonization of the Moon. They are centered on a series of contract awards to various space companies meant to deliver increasingly more hardware to the satellite, as the Americans are racing to become the first in the world to establish an extraterrestrial outpost.
We'll get to all of that in due time, but I'll start with something that hasn't been in the news all that often: a nuclear-powered Moon rover called the Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration.
That would be PROMISE for short, a six-wheeled machine packed to the teeth with science instruments and technology demonstrations that are meant to provide us with a better understanding of the place some of us will use to live and work in the near future.
The rover is being developed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, but not in the usual fashion, from the ground up,. Instead, engineers are using spare flight components and engineering test models that have already been used on the Curiosity and Perseverance Mars rovers.
This approach, says the agency, makes the development of the rover cheaper than it would have otherwise been, but also faster, as some of the parts and processes that will go into it are already available.
The PROMISE will carry with it to the Moon a drill that will help it extract regolith from some three feet (one meter) below the lunar surface, and spectrometers which it will use to analyze the material in search of ice and other resources.
It will also be equipped with temperature and radiation sensors and visible light cameras. Most importantly, though, the rover will carry to the Moon a next-gen radiation-tolerant computer, the High Performance Spaceflight Computing.
Partially autonomous, the PROMISE will be powered by a yet-undetailed nuclear system that can keep it operational in the harsh conditions of the lunar night or in the permanently shadowed regions of the Moon at the South Pole .
Aside from looking for resources that could be used to sustain a human presence there, the rover will also scout for other potential landing places for the huge number of upcoming Moon missions.
The space agency has already decided on when the rover will be launched, and who will send it to the Moon. The departure time for the PROMISE mission is the end of 2028, and the launch rocket will be a Blue Origin rocket. To get the machine down to the surface, a Mark 1 lander of the same company will be employed.
NASA will spend between $94 million and $140 million to send the rover on its way. We'll keep an eye on the mission and return with updates once more is revealed.

1970 Ford Mustang Mach 1 R-Code 428 Cobra Jet Begs for Restoration After Years in Hiding
28 photos
Photo: eBay seller hbmustangs
I don’t know about you, but every time I see a 1970 Mustang, I think about Ford’s marketing campaign that insisted on how buying a Mustang could have changed your life. And this Mach 1 did just that, making me think of those times when Ford thought it was cool to tell guys that buying a new car would have helped them for… you know.
“Marc Muccino’s coaching career was a big ‘zero’ until he bought his Mustang SportsRoof. Now it’s a whole new ball game,” Ford said in one of these Mustang booklets, showing a man surrounded by attractive women.
I do admit that the 1970 Mustang was a gorgeous car, despite not sporting all that many changes from the previous. This made sense, considering the 1969 model year witnessed the introduction of a major makeover, but the 1970 model year somehow brought this release to maturity.
This Mach 1 is here because it needs a second chance to re-become this awesome car that once turned heads everywhere. We don’t know much about its past, but it certainly looks like it’s been sitting for more than just a couple of years in a place away from humanity.
It needs a complete restoration, and the thing that caught my attention was the R-coded setup. This car was once powered by the 428 Cobra Jet, the second-best engine you could get in 1970.
Photo: eBay seller hbmustangs Ford offered not one, not two, but nine different engine choices in 1970. Two sixes - a 200 with 120 horsepower and a 250 with 155 horsepower - were specifically aimed at those buyers who cared more about the looks than the power under the hood.
The 302 rated at 220 horsepower marked the foray into the V8 business, while the Boss version of the same engine provided more adrenaline behind the wheel thanks to an increase to 290 horsepower.
The 351 was available in two versions. The two-barrel configuration went as high as 250 horsepower, while the four-barrel sibling produced 300 horsepower.
Then, the big guys showed up.
The 428 Cobra produced 335 horsepower, but Ford also offered the same output on the 428 Cobra Jet. Both engines could only be ordered with a SelectShift or a 4-speed manual close-ratio transmission.
The top choice was the 429 Boss with 375 horsepower.
Photo: eBay seller hbmustangs This Mach 1 was once powered by the Cobra Jet, but that’s no longer the case today. The only thing you’ll find in the engine bay is a lot of fresh air. The seller doesn’t share additional details, but I wouldn’t be surprised to learn that the engine and the transmission were both removed to be donated to another Mach 1 that was being restored.
The car has clearly been sitting for a while, and the owner says it from the very beginning. It “needs a lot of rust repairs,” and there’s no doubt this is true.
This isn’t an easy project, especially if you want to restore it to factory specifications. There’s another reason why you’ll want to stick with the original settings, as the car was wearing the rare Pastel Blue paired with a blue interior.
And speaking about the interior, it’s mostly complete, though it goes without saying that using everything for restoration wouldn’t be possible. My advice is to call the seller and maybe ask for more details, and if you don’t live very far, you should also go there in person and see the car with your own eyes.
Photo: eBay seller hbmustangs Otherwise, it’s hard to be disappointed if you know what to expect. This Mustang is a massive project that would be worth the effort once done right.
This wasn’t an affordable car and still isn’t. The hardtop was the most affordable Mustang version in 1970, carrying a starting price of $2,721, while the fastback was next with a base price of $2,771. The Grand was next with $2,926 for the base configuration, while the top choices, the Mach 1 and the convertible, surpassed the $3K threshold.
The convertible started at $3,025, while the Mach 1 was available from $3,271. The more options you added, the higher the price went, so for example, if you wanted the top 429 with 375 horsepower, you had to pay no more, no less than $1,208 more on your Mustang.
Photo: eBay seller hbmustangs This Mustang can be yours for $12,850, but the seller has also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay, so you can try your luck and see if they accept your offer if you have another deal in mind. The car is parked in Aragon, Georgia, and you should also consider shipping costs, given that the engine is no longer there, so the car does not run.
The listing will expire in 24 days, so you have all the time in the world to convince your wife that you need this car and the seller to accept your offer.

Bentley Honors Past Veterans With Two 2026 Remembrance One-Offs: Bentayga EWB and a Supersports
11 photos
Photo: Bentley
Although they share the same date, November 11, Remembrance Day and Veterans Day are not the exact same commemorative event: both have the same WWI roots but diverge a bit in modern culture.
They were instituted to mark the Armistice Day of the end of the First World War, as hostilities ceased "at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month" in 1918. However, Remembrance Day is a tradition of Commonwealth Nations – the UK, Canada, Australia, and others – focused mainly on the veterans who lost their lives in the line of duty, which is basically similar to the US Memorial Day.
On the other hand, Veterans Day in the United States is aimed at honoring all American military veterans from all ages, both still living or dead. Alas, since Bentley wanted to unite people with a “symbol of remembrance and belonging,” we’re not going to be picky and share with you these two commemorative automobiles: a one-of-a-kind Bentayga EWB Artenara edition and Bentley Supersports.
They were both designed specifically to honor Remembrance Day as unique creations that were curated by the Bentley Design team in collaboration with BeReady, an internal employee resource network at Bentley Motors aimed at supporting military veterans, active reservists, and their families as part of the five Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) networks active within the company.
This is the fifth initiative for the Remembrance Day, with the one from 2025 also a one-of-a-kind Bentayga EWB Azure specifically designed as a tribute focused on the Battle of Britain and honoring “the 17 colleagues who tragically lost their lives whilst building the Merlin Aero Engine when the bomb dropped over Crewe 85 years ago and honors all those who have served.”
Back in 2026, Bentley again paid tribute during an on-site Remembrance event with dignitaries from the Ministry of Defence, the local Royal British Legion and the Crewe Town Council, again honoring the memory of the 17 people “who lost their lives serving the nation during wartime.” The newest tribute to the Armed Forces is two specially commissioned cars, a Bentayga Extended Wheelbase Artenara and a Bentley Supersports .
The Bentley Artenara special edition was launched in March 2026 as a tribute to the crossover SUV's name: Roque Bentayga, a rock formation on the island of Gran Canaria. The Extended Wheelbase model comes with the Bentayga’s 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 with 542 hp, while the Supersports is a special model based on the fourth-generation Bentley Continental GT Coupe that has returned this year after a near decade-long hiatus as an ICE-only Conti GT with the V8 packing no less than 657 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque or 800 Nm.
Bentley and its colleagues affectionately nickname the Remembrance models as their ‘Poppy’ cars, and they participated in a series of activities, like the on-site Remembrance service in Crewe, Mission Motorsport's Race of Remembrance at the Anglesey circuit, and more. They were created by Bentley's design team together with BeReady and take inspiration from “John McCrae's iconic poem In Flanders Fields.”
It’s not only a reflection on loss, but the poem is also dubbed “a message from the fallen to the living, reminding future generations of the sacrifices made in defense of freedom and the responsibility to carry their legacy forward.”
The bespoke exterior artwork uses poppies and symbolic imagery, with poppies “blooming across a battlefield and larks soaring overhead” to “symbolize life enduring through adversity, while the central artwork honors those who made the ultimate sacrifice, remembering them not as distant heroes but as ordinary people who loved and were loved.”
Additionally, many colleagues from Bentley’s manufacturing team crocheted handmade poppies to help raise funds for the Royal British Legion. Back in America, General Motors announced $14 million in support for active-duty service members, veterans, and their families with pledges to Stars, Stripes & Skilled Trades ($3 million), one million for Hiring Our Heroes (HOH), no less than $6 million for Tunnels to Towers, and more. Looking for a biopharma job in New Jersey? Jobs on BioSpace increased year over year in October, and there are hundreds of open positions posted now.
Job postings live for New Jersey on the BioSpace website have bounced up and down in 2026 and dropped 25% from September to October. Still, there has been year-over-year improvement. Jobs live for the state, located within the Pharm Country Hotbed , jumped 22% from October 2025 to October 2026.
If you’re interested in working at a biopharma in New Jersey, there are around 300 positions posted on BioSpace now. Check out the open jobs at these 10 companies.
Legend Biotech has around 50 positions available. Jobs include scientist, immunoassays, in Somerset; senior specialist, quality IT, in Bridgewater; and senior engineer in Raritan.
Sanofi has over 40 open roles in Morristown. Positions include real world evidence scientific lead; global transplant medical lead, pipeline; and digital architect.
Insmed has around 40 positions available in Bridgewater. Jobs include associate scientist, drug formulation; director, translational bioanalytical sciences; and scientist, discovery pharmacology.
Regeneron has nearly 40 open roles in Warren. Positions include senior manager, clinical supply operations; manager, clinical study lead (oncology); and senior director, global patient safety-rare disease.
GenScript has around two dozen positions available in Piscataway. Jobs include senior scientist, product development-life science and biotech reagents; lab technician; and order management associate scientist.
Amgen has nearly 20 open roles. Positions include medical science liaison-bone health-NJ in Newark; account manager/specialty account manager-IgG4 (rare disease)-Wayne, NJ, in Paterson; and field reimbursement manager-Newark in Newark.
Novo has about 20 positions available in Plainsboro. Jobs include security engineer III; director, United States operations quality audits and inspections; and category management manager-clinical services.
AbbVie has over a dozen open roles. Positions include senior scientist, I: biocompatibility, in Branchburg; associate, clinical data systems, in Florham Park; and associate director, statistics, in Florham Park.
InVitro Cell Research has around a dozen positions available in Englewood. Jobs include principal scientist-cancer early detection; scientist, bioinformatics; and scientist, functional genomics.
Tris Pharma has about a dozen open roles in Monmouth Junction. Positions include AR&D scientist I/II; QA R&D chemist I; and senior quality systems engineer/APQR lead.

This Is What the Facelifted 2028 BMW M5 Will Look Like – Rendering
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
The modern-day BMW M5 has started to age quite nicely, though “nice” isn’t the best word to describe it. Chances are we will look at it a few years from now just like we do at the E60 generation from the Bangle era, at least on the outside, because the screen-filled interior is not exactly future proof.
However, just when the current M5 has started to look a bit better, BMW will retire it. Not for good, obviously, because it will be replaced by the facelifted iteration. We have spotted it numerous times, doing its thing in various environments, and our previous encounter with a camouflaged prototype dates back to late October 2026. That exact prototype has been used by Kolesa’ Nikita Chuyko to create this set of renderings.
The digital illustrations shared in the gallery are on the realistic side of things, because this is what the upcoming BMW M5 will look like once the wraps officially come off. The model has gone down the Neue Klasse route, both inside and out, and it is one of those “love it or hate it” cases, because there is really no middle ground. Thus, whether you like it or not, you’d better get used to the design, as you will eventually see it in the flesh once the car starts reaching dealers worldwide.
Compared to the outgoing iteration, the facelifted BMW M5 features slimmer headlights with an entirely new daytime running light signature. The main clusters do not protrude that much into the front fenders, and have been further extended to the grille. The latter part is now slimmer and wider than before, and it is separated in the middle by a vertical slat painted in the same color as the rest of the body.
Photo: Kolesa The front bumper has become even more aggressive. The double air intakes in the middle are larger, the side vents are bigger, and there is an apron with blades on the sides that is visible in these digital illustrations. The hood is now a lot smaller than before, and the front fenders have been redesigned . Further back, we can see the same doors, handles, windows, mirrors, side skirts, rear three-quarter panels, and the charging port on the left front fender, because the model is still a plug-in hybrid.
The wheels have been virtually sourced from the latest scooped prototype, complete with the yellow brake calipers, and even the red paint finish, which is a bit darker on this rendered car. The back end looks more evolutionary than the front fascia. Here, we can see that the taillights feature different graphics, the bumper has been tweaked, and the rear diffuser has been replaced with a much sportier-looking one. A discreet ducktail spoiler still adorns it, and the M5 badge still sits above the right taillight. The signature quad exhaust tips are pretty much the same as before.
If you want to see what the facelifted BMW M5 looks like inside, then all you have to do is look at other brand-new Bimmers, such as the 3 Series, the i3, X5, 7 Series, and so on. What does this mean? Well, the Panoramic iDrive pillar-to-pillar display stretching at the bottom of the windshield, alongside the free-floating infotainment screen. An optional passenger display will probably be available, and the steering wheel will likely become quirkier looking.
Photo: Kolesa
There is no official word about the powertrain so far, but since this is a facelift and not a new generation, we can say that the plug-in hybrid 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 will live on. Whether it will become punchier or not is a question that will be answered in due course. Meanwhile, we will remind you that the current BMW M5 has 717 hp (727 ps/535 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque combined, hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 seconds for the Sedan and 3.5 seconds for the Touring.
By the way, both body styles are on sale in the United States of America, in case you forgot, and they are 2027 model year cars. The M5 Sedan has an MSRP of $123,300, and the M5 Touring starts at $125,300. The upcoming M5 will likely be a bit pricier, and we expect it to arrive at dealers nationwide for the 2028 model year. This means that the unveiling should take place a few months from now, though for the moment, the debut date is being kept close to BMW’s chest.
So, there you have it folks, another BMW that’s entering the Neue Klasse realm, and to be honest, it does not look horrible on the outside . Well, at least not when comparing it to other Neue Klasse vehicles. However, the bland-looking interior filled with technology is one of the things that makes it controversial, this writer believes. Well, this and the fact that it will continue to be slower than the old F90 M5 if the automaker does not boost the output. Would you see yourself driving a 2028 BMW M5?

October marked the first time this year there was an increase in both the number of biotech and pharma companies trimming their workforces and the number of affected employees when compared to 2025. Still, it’s highly unlikely 2026 layoffs will come close to matching the downsizing seen last year.
While October showed a year-over-year increase in the number of biopharmas making or planning workforce cuts and in total affected employees, layoffs should steeply drop from 2025 to 2026, based on BioSpace tallies.
Last month, three more employers trimmed or expected to trim staff compared to October 2025, and overall cuts impacted 43% more people. It was the first time in 2026 that there was a year-over-year increase in the number of companies making or planning cuts. It was the third time the number of affected employees rose. Year over year, there were also jumps in February (+283%) and May (+47%).
Aside from October, the only other month in 2026 when more companies made or planned layoffs was March. There were three months when more employees were affected: February (3,773), March (2,417) and May (6,956).
Still, there is a strong downward trend in layoffs from 2025 to 2026. Last year, 200 biopharmas cut or planned to cut 43,242 employees. This year’s total through October is 99 companies and 19,538 people. To reach last year’s numbers, two dramatic increases must happen this month and next month. First, at least 101 companies that did not previously have layoffs this year must make or plan layoffs, or be newly reported as having done so earlier this year. (Some companies disclose cuts retrospectively rather than as they happen.) Second, newly reported workforce reductions by all biopharmas must affect over 23,700 employees.
October brings major shakeups at 6 companies
Of the 15 biotech and pharma companies with made or planned layoffs in October, six are cutting at least 50% of their workforces: Aviceda Therapeutics, Artiva Biotherapeutics, Caribou Biosciences, LENZ Therapeutics, Enlivex and EyePoint.
Aviceda Therapeutics
Aviceda Therapeutics is undergoing the most dramatic change. The Cambridge, Massachusetts–based biotech is winding down its business . The company employed 51 to 200 people, according to its LinkedIn profile.
As to why Aviceda is shuttering, Endpoints News reported that a LinkedIn post said the business made its decision “due to clinical trial results.” The company was developing therapies to treat retinal diseases.
An Aviceda asset, AVD-104, missed its primary endpoint in a Phase 2b clinical trial last year, but the company planned to advance it into Phase 3 confirmatory studies, the biotech announced in December 2025.
Artiva Biotherapeutics
Artiva Biotherapeutics is laying off 94% of its workforce and exploring strategic options that could include a merger, business combination, sale or licensing of assets, or dissolution and liquidation, the company announced Oct. 27. That move will affect 131 employees effective Dec. 31, according to a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice .
In addition to the layoffs, the San Diego–based biotech is ending development of lead candidate AlloNK following two patient deaths and questions about the clinical response durability of that candidate. Artiva had been evaluating the cell therapy for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases.
Caribou Biosciences
Caribou Biosciences is also cutting most of its workforce, letting go of 87 people effective Dec. 7, according to a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice . The Berkeley, California–based company had 97 employees as of Feb. 27, meaning the layoffs could affect 90% of its staff.
Like Aviceda, Caribou is considering strategic alternatives, which it announced could include, but are not limited to, a merger, acquisition, business combination or other strategic transaction involving the biotech and its assets.
Caribou attributed its layoffs and exploration of strategic options, as well as its decision to discontinue further development of its clinical-stage pipeline, to a financing freeze in the CAR T space. The company has two active assets: the CD19-targeting vispa-cel for B cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma and the anti-BCMA CB-011 for multiple myeloma.
LENZ Therapeutics
While LENZ Therapeutics’ layoffs are not as extensive as those at Aviceda, Artiva and Caribou, the company is nonetheless eliminating most of its employees. The Solana Beach, California–based biotech will cut about 75% of its workforce, leaving around 40 full-time employees, as disclosed in an SEC filing . Departing employees include President and CEO Eef Schimmelpennink, who exits Dec. 1.
LENZ, which developed Vizz, an aceclidine-based eye drop for the treatment of presbyopia, attributed the move to a strategic reorganization meant to prioritize consumer marketing, allocate capital to maximize sales growth and reduce operating expenses. The biotech disclosed the strategy shift alongside third quarter earnings that fell short of expectations .
Enlivex
Enlivex is cutting about 60% of its workforce, the company announced Oct. 19. The Nes Ziona, Israel–based biotech had 34 full-time employees as of Dec. 31, 2025, meaning the layoffs could affect around 20 people.
The company attributed the workforce reduction to a restructuring initiative meant to cut costs and channel resources toward the midstage development of Allocetra, an off-the-shelf cell therapy for knee osteoarthritis. To help save money, Enlivex is lowering senior leader compensation packages. CEO Oren Hershkovitz will take a 40% pay cut and the management team a 20% compensation reduction.
EyePoint
EyePoint is roughly halving its team with a 53% staff cut , the biotech announced Oct. 19. The layoffs will hit 105 employees in Massachusetts at the Watertown headquarters and Northbridge manufacturing facility, according to a Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notice . The cuts are effective Dec. 31, 2026, to Jan. 31, 2027.
The layoffs are part of a strategic reprioritization following a disappointing readout for investigational tyrosine kinase inhibitor duravyu in wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The Watertown-based biotech is ending the asset’s pivotal wet AMD trials early, EyePoint said in a separate announcement . It will now focus resources on its late-stage program for duravyu in diabetic macular edema (DME).
GSK cuts will affect the most employees
While the six companies above are cutting large percentages of their workforces, GSK’s layoffs last month will affect the most people. The U.K. pharma is eliminating more than 1,200 roles —as many as 1,217—in Belgium. The cuts are part of a three-year, $2.5 billion global restructuring meant to reallocate capital and resources toward GSK’s late-stage pipeline and research and development efforts, a company spokesperson told BioSpace .
The layoffs will hit the pharma’s Rixensart, Wavre and Gembloux sites, Belgium news publication L’Echo reported.
Layoff numbers exclude contract development and manufacturing organizations, contract research organizations, tools and services businesses and medical device firms. To tally the cuts, BioSpace compiles data for known workforce reductions. The number of employees affected is identified or estimated through confirmation from company officials as well as information in company press releases, Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act notices, SEC filings and media outlets’ reports.
Not all companies disclose downsizing, and some share only the percentage of staff affected. Some biopharmas provide total numbers retrospectively rather than disclosing individual workforce reductions as they happen.

New-Gen Feature Coming to Apple Maps, Making ETAs More Accurate Than in Google Maps
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Navigation apps are getting all kinds of new-gen gimmicks, such as aerial views and cyclist warnings, but Apple is working on something that will certainly come in handy for drivers.
The fruit-named company is reportedly preparing parking-aware ETAs, which means that the application would take into account the time you spend parking and walking to calculate your ETA. This means you’ll get more accurate ETAs than in any other application, such as Waze, where the time of arrival is exclusively based on traffic conditions to reach a destination.
Like all the other navigation apps out there, Apple Maps uses a simple system to determine your ETA to a destination.
When you define the address where you want to drive, Apple Maps checks the distance, speed limits, and traffic data to determine how much time you’ll spend on the road to the destination. This ETA refers exclusively to the time you spend behind the wheel going from point A to point B, without considering any other factors, such as the time you spend when you park your car.
That’s going to change if a feature that Apple is currently working on behind closed doors makes its way to the production channel.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution A recent post on X from @itspdfu indicates that Apple is developing a feature that would measure how long you spend near your destination for parking and how much time you add to your journey walking to the destination. This is possible using background location and motion data, so your iPhone would collect the necessary data to determine how much time you need to reach a destination in addition to the driving time.
This feature comes in handy for two reasons. The first one is related to the parking job, as finding a parking spot in a busy area isn’t always easy. Apple Maps could collect data related to parking and offer an estimated time of arrival that would also include such information, making it easier for users to determine the time when they will arrive at the destination - when this destination is not a location on the street but a building or another location not reachable by car.
For example, if you need to arrive at a meeting at an office building, Apple Maps would also take into account the parking time and how much you’d walk from your car to the building itself. This way, you’ll know more accurately when you arrive at the meeting location.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution This feature is currently in the works, and there is no guarantee that it’ll ever make its way to production. Ideas like this one come and go, and I wouldn’t be surprised to see Apple dropping it. However, considering it has already been added in the iOS 27.3 code, this could be a sign that the feature has made it past the drawing board and could eventually land for all users.
Meanwhile, Google Maps is also offering a similar feature, though it won’t show ETA based on parking data. The application can highlight a building on the map when your destination is that building and provide walking directions from the parking spot to its location.
Like Apple Maps, Google Maps also offers walking and driving directions, so this feature combines both modes for uninterrupted navigation. Once users arrive at the destination where they are supposed to park their cars, Google Maps shows the walking directions, so they continue the journey without entering a new address in the application.
Waze is the only application that can’t get such capabilities because it’s exclusively aimed at drivers. Waze does not support walking, so it always shows the ETA as the point on the map where you are supposed to drive. It can also indicate nearby parking, but it doesn’t offer any walking directions afterwards.
Apple Maps is still working on the detailed city experience that includes more detailed maps, improved navigation, and a redesigned CarPlay experience. The rollout of this feature started in 2021 but is still underway, with Apple seemingly taking its time to bring the new maps to more locations worldwide.
The highly detailed maps were supposed to turn Apple Maps into a fully-featured Google Maps alternative, but considering the slow rollout - most of which is aimed at American regions - many users decided to stick with Google Maps.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Google itself is now in the process of rolling out a similar update called immersive navigation . Google Maps is getting detailed maps with crosswalks and sidewalks, as well as see-through overpasses and 3D buildings similar to those integrated into Apple’s detailed city experience. Google’s new experience is live in the United States and Canada and should arrive in the rest of the world at some point next month.
Apple has so far remained tight-lipped on this new feature spotted in Apple Maps, and I wouldn’t expect the company to say anything about it until it goes live for production users. Apple may be working on parking-aware ETAs. iOS 27.3 adds a TimeToPark flag. When enabled, CoreRoutine uses background location and motion data to measure how long you spent near your destination before parking, and how long you walked afterwards. It saves both metrics per trip, grouped by day of the week and hour. The feature can only be enabled on internal installs, and no Maps feature uses the data yet. — pdfu (@itspdfu) November 9, 2026

Auto Supplier ZF Reveals the High Revolution Electric Drive That Spins at 30,000 RPM
9 photos
Photo: ZF
As the world sinks deeper and deeper into the era of the electric car, the technologies that have powered the early iterations of these vehicles are rapidly evolving. Most of the research was until now focused on batteries, so that they can deliver more range and less range anxiety, but now electric motors and the associated hardware are becoming the focus of research and development.
Several important evolutions in this field have come to light in recent weeks, and we'll focus here on something called the High Revolution Drive. It is a piece of technology made by German supplier ZF , and designed to spin extremely fast, while being lighter and smaller than most existing hardware.
How fast does this thing spin, you ask? Well, ZF talks about 30,000 rpm, which is roughly double what most present solutions are capable of today. Despite this, the design is 25 percent smaller and about the same percentage lighter than the platform it is based on, ZF's Select, which normally spins at 18,000 rpm.
The company says that, on top of all of the above, the magnet mass has dropped by 50 percent, and the system is capable of 93 percent efficiency, even at high rotational speeds and with a high gear ratio.
The 3-in-1 electric drive comprises a two-stage helical cylindrical gear transmission with an 18:1 ratio to send torque to the wheels, and it plays in the 268-horsepower class. Torque levels are enormous, with ZF saying they stand at 3,500 Nm.
The Germans say they imagined the High Revolution Drive with specific applications in mind: high-volume passenger vehicles with drive outputs between 200 and 268 hp. It has been designed in such a way as to be able to be integrated into both 400- and 800-volt systems.
For these rides, ZF promises not only the same amount of power in a smaller (and subsequently cheaper) electric drive , but also an increased range for the electric vehicle it is meant to serve. We're not provided with the numbers that make it clearer what that means.
Because it is based on the existing Select platform, which is about to be integrated into a number of upcoming electric cars, and uses existing technologies, the High Revolution Drive does not require significant investments from automakers to be adopted.
It's likely it will be a while, though, before we get to see the ZF High Revolution Drive in action on commercial vehicles. ZF admitted it is already in talks with several automakers it does not name to produce the technology, but at the same time it adds that it doesn't plan to start making it before the 2030s.
As with all other innovations, we'll keep an eye on this piece of hardware and report back once we know more about it and its capabilities.

2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition Rides Low and Puts 1,000 HP to the Ground
15 photos
Photo: Fox Factory Vehicles
The 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition takes Las Vegas by storm. Dressed to impress at the 2026 SEMA Show, it is a limited-production, lowered street truck that throws caution to the wind with up to 1,000 horsepower and looks like it eats tarmac for breakfast.
When everyone builds lifted trucks, standing sky-high and dwarfing just about any vehicle out there, the all-new 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee Foose Edition drives in the opposite direction, full speed ahead. It rides low, on 22-inch Foose-designed wheels with Michelin high-performance street tires, showing its intent from the get-go: it is built for the pavement and drag-strip performance.
The truck received a bespoke front splitter, side skirts, a tailgate spoiler, custom bedside graphics and signature hood emblems, with the latter designed specifically for the variants that come with the 6.2-liter supercharged V8. Foose-designed upholstery made its way into the cabin, along with interior badging and all-weather floor mats, while a WeatherTech tonneau cover protects the cargo.
Buyers can choose between two configurations, and both are equipped with a Whipple-supercharged HEMI V8. The Ram 1500 Rumble Bee 392 Track Pack comes with the 6.4-liter HEMI dialed up to produce 705 horsepower (715 metric horsepower) from the standard 470 horsepower (477 metric horsepower).
Photo: Fox Factory Vehicles But the biggest departure from stock is what Foose did to the Rumble Bee SRT, as the 6.2-liter HEMI now goes as far as 1,000 horsepower (1,014 metric horsepower) from the stock 777 horsepower (787 metric horsepower). However, the figures are currently just targeted outputs and are subject to final validation before production.
The list of performance upgrades includes a twin-screw supercharger setup, an oversized heat exchanger to manage thermal loads, and a dual-outlet MagnaFlow exhaust with Direct Connection tips, roaring out all the HEMI drama. The Foose Edition commands a significant premium over the standard lineup in exchange for all the bespoke bodywork, lowered coil-over Ridetech hardware, and massive power.
The firm has yet to release the new performance details. When stock, the Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT rockets from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.4 seconds and runs the quarter mile in 11.6 seconds on its way to a top speed of 170 mph (274 kph). That's already supercar territory, even without the Foose upgrade.
FOX Factory Vehicles lists the starting price at $154,990 for the 705-horsepower 392 Track Pack base model, which is nearly double the $79,995 of the stock model (excluding destination). In the meantime, the price of the almighty Rumble Bee SRT with 1,000 horsepower has yet to be announced. The standard Rumble Bee SRT is a $94,995 deal or $97,790 with the destination charge.
So you shouldn't be surprised if Foose Design makes that double, too. Regardless of the price, both trucks come with a factory-backed three-year or 36,000-mile warranty. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Chip Foose (@chipfooseofficial)

BYD Integrates Solar Power, Energy Storage, Flash Charging, Robotic Charging System Into a Facility
7 photos
Photo: BYD
BYD , the multinational high-tech company established in 1994 with the clear goal of pursuing Tesla's place of world EV dominance, is taking a new step toward the path of becoming an all-in-one provider of new energy ‘greatness.’
The Chinese brand was initially a rechargeable battery maker, but a little more than three decades later it has invested in automobiles, rail transit, new energy, and electronics, with over 30 industrial parks in China, the United States, Canada, Japan, Brazil, Hungary, and India. BYD Auto was founded a little later, in 2003, but through “significant technological advancements” like the Blade Battery , the DM-i and DM-p hybrid technology, or the Super e-Platform, it has quickly risen the ranks to become the world’s largest EV maker since 2025.
Now, BYD has announced the creation of a new installation in the Abu Dhabi desert that features a new type of integrated charging system, “bringing together solar power generation, energy storage, Flash Charging and robotic charging for the first time in a single solution.” The system aims to mix the use and generation of renewable energy with the company’s proprietary ultra-fast charging and automated vehicle technology, thus establishing a new type of approach to the charging experience.
The station has BYD’s Flash Charging technology, which enables charging times to move closer than ever to conventional refueling, with the time needed to go from 10% to 70% state-of-charge being an advertised five minutes, followed by a potential 10% to 97% in nine minutes. The new integrated system combines the proprietary Flash Charging station with solar power generation, energy storage, and even robotic charging.
More precisely, the installation uses BYD’s Solar-Storage-Charging (SSC) system, which links solar energy generation to battery storage and Flash Charging. Basically, the local solar energy is captured and stored on-site to be used for vehicle charging as needed. The SSC supports independent operation from the grid, opening up flexibility in locations where grid access is limited.
Of course, BYD took the new SSC installation to the Abu Dhabi desert, where the climate is a haven for solar charging – the area is characterized “by intense sunlight, high temperatures and scarce rainfall.” Additionally, the system integrates a robotic arm that can take care of the vehicle’s charging connection, “automatically locating the charging port, opening its cover and inserting the connector.”
It uses both visual guidance and force feedback so that the arm can ensure accurate alignment and a secure connection to BYD’s Flash Charging system. Additionally, BYD wants to integrate the robotic charging with Automated Valet Parking, so that “drivers can simply exit the vehicle, lock it, and walk away while the car autonomously navigates to a designated charging space,” where the robotic arm takes over to connect the vehicle and start the charging process.
